# Realtor.com Scraper

<!-- This README is generated by .github/scripts/docs.py from the scraper code, its results/ folder and .github/scrapers.json: change those and run the script instead of editing it. -->

[![tests](https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers/raw/ci-status/badges/realtorcom-scraper.svg)](https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers/blob/ci-status/status/realtorcom-scraper.md)

Example scraper that collects property listing data from Realtor.com, written in Python with the [Scrapfly](https://scrapfly.io/) web scraping API. Part of [scrapfly-scrapers](../README.md).

- **Guide:** [How to Scrape Realtor.com - Real Estate Property Data](https://scrapfly.io/blog/posts/how-to-scrape-realtorcom)
- **Code:** [`realtorcom.py`](realtorcom.py) · **Example run:** [`run.py`](run.py) · **Tests:** [`test.py`](test.py)
- **Sample output:** [Property pages](results/property.json) · [Search pages](results/search.json) · [Feed pages](results/feed.json)

## What it scrapes

- Realtor.com property listing data
- Realtor.com search results
- Realtor.com property change feeds (RSS)

## Functions

- `scrape_property(url)` → `List[Dict]`: scrape realtor.com's property page for property data
- `scrape_search(state, city, max_pages=None)` → `List[Dict]`: scrape realtor.com's search and find properties for given query. Paginate to max pages if provided
- `scrape_feed(url)` → `Dict[str, datetime]`: scrapes atom RSS feed and returns all entries in "url:publish date" format

The functions are `async`: run them with `asyncio.run(...)` or `await` them.

### Example

The inputs are the examples of [`run.py`](run.py) (long lists cut short):

```python
import asyncio
import realtorcom


async def main():
    property = await realtorcom.scrape_property(
        "https://www.realtor.com/realestateandhomes-detail/12355-Attlee-Dr_Houston_TX_77077_M70330-35605",
    )
    search = await realtorcom.scrape_search("CA", "San-Francisco", max_pages=2)
    feed = await realtorcom.scrape_feed("https://cdn.realtor.ca/sitemap/realtorsitemap/sitemap.xml")


asyncio.run(main())
```

## Output

The functions return plain dictionaries and lists. Fields of the sample output (top-level keys of the first item):

- [`results/property.json`](results/property.json): `id`, `slug`, `url`, `status`, `tags`, `sold_date`, `sold_price`, `list_date`, `list_price`, `list_price_last_change`, `details`, `flags`, `local`, `location`, `agent`, `advertisers`, `tax_history`, `history`, `photos`, `phones`, `features`

## Scrapfly settings

`BASE_CONFIG` in [`realtorcom.py`](realtorcom.py) holds the default settings of the requests, see the [Scrape API documentation](https://scrapfly.io/docs/scrape-api/getting-started):

- `unblocker` = `True`: Scrapfly's [Unblocker](https://scrapfly.io/docs/scrape-api/unblocker), its anti-bot bypass
- `country` = `"US"`: country of the proxy

## Quick start

Requires Python 3.10+ and [Poetry](https://python-poetry.org/docs/#installation).

```shell
git clone https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers.git
cd scrapfly-scrapers/realtorcom-scraper
export SCRAPFLY_KEY="YOUR SCRAPFLY KEY"   # from https://scrapfly.io/dashboard
poetry install --no-root
poetry run python run.py                  # example scrape, saves its output in ./results
poetry run pytest test.py                 # the tests of this scraper
```

Tests: `test_property_scraping`, `test_search_scraping`, `test_feed_scraping`; run one with `poetry run pytest test.py -k <test>`. `run.py` and the tests scrape the live website, so they use Scrapfly credits.
